record.context_brief: Finite-measurement identification of an insulating crack.
record.original_question: Let Omega be a bounded connected open subset of R^3, let Sigma be an orientable smooth two-dimensional surface compactly contained in Omega with simple closed boundary, and interpret Sigma as an insulating crack. For each prescribed boundary current density psi on ∂Omega with zero average, let u solve Delta u = 0 in Omega \ Sigma, with normal derivative grad u · nu = 0 on either side of Sigma and grad u · nu = psi on ∂Omega. Do there exist finitely many boundary current profiles psi_1, ..., psi_N such that, if u_1, ..., u_N are the corresponding potentials, the boundary measurements u_1|_{∂Omega}, ..., u_N|_{∂Omega} uniquely determine Sigma?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 (The insulating crack problem). To find appropriately chosen current profiles ψ1, . . . ψN such that, letting u1, . . . uN be the corresponding potentials, the boundary measurements u1|∂Ω, . . . uN |∂Ω uniquely determine Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded connected open set with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $\Sigma \Subset \Omega$ be an orientable smooth two-dimensional surface with simple closed boundary, interpreted as an insulating crack. For a prescribed boundary current density $\psi \in L^2(\partial\Omega)$ with $\int_{\partial\Omega}\psi\,dS = 0$, let $u$ be the (weak) solution of
\[
\Delta u = 0 \text{ in } \Omega \setminus \Sigma, \qquad \nabla u \cdot \nu = 0 \text{ on both sides of } \Sigma, \qquad \nabla u \cdot \nu = \psi \text{ on } \partial\Omega,
\]
normalized by $\int_{\partial\Omega} u\,dS = 0$. The question is: do there exist a finite integer $N$ and boundary current profiles $\psi_1, \dots, \psi_N$ (possibly depending on a priori bounds on $\Sigma$ but not on $\Sigma$ itself within an admissible class) such that the corresponding boundary potentials $u_1|_{\partial\Omega}, \dots, u_N|_{\partial\Omega}$ uniquely determine the surface $\Sigma$?
artifact.status_search_result: In three dimensions, uniqueness of crack identification from finitely many boundary measurements is established only in restricted cases (e.g., flat insulating cracks via two measurements), while general 3D uniqueness results require the full Neumann-to-Dirichlet map. The problem of identifying a general (curved) insulating surface in 3D from finitely many boundary measurements appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Stability and Uniqueness for the Crack Identification Problem
status_evidence.snippet: For both perfectly conducting and perfectly insulating cracks, exactly two measurements suffice for unique detection, though for insulating cracks they must be flat.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-measurement uniqueness for 3D insulating cracks is known only when the crack is flat.

status_evidence.title: A Review of Selected Works on Crack Identification
status_evidence.snippet: Few uniqueness results exist in the 3D framework, and they all require the knowledge of all the possible measurements.
status_evidence.claim: General 3D uniqueness results require all boundary measurements, indicating the finite-measurement case is open.
